claims.text: An anonymous tip alerted McDonald's board to Easterbrook's relationships with employees
The board conducted an investigation with outside counsel before making a decision
Easterbrook was dismissed without cause on November 3, 2019 for violating company policy
Chris Kempczinski was appointed as Easterbrook's successor

outcome.summary: Easterbrook was dismissed without cause in November 2019. In 2020, McDonald's sued Easterbrook to recover severance and equity, alleging he lied about the scope of his relationships. In 2021, McDonald's reported additional evidence of relationships with three more employees. The case was settled in 2023 with Easterbrook agreeing to pay McDonald's an undisclosed sum.

timeline.event: McDonald's board learns of Easterbrook's relationships with employees through an anonymous tip
Board begins investigation with help of outside counsel
Board concludes Easterbrook violated company policy and dismisses him without cause
Chris Kempczinski named as new CEO

title: Steve Easterbrook dismissed as McDonald's CEO
trigger: McDonald's board dismissed CEO Steve Easterbrook after determining he had violated company policy by engaging in consensual relationships with company employees.
